items.title: William and Kate reflect on 'enduring' UK-India ties with Modi
items.summary: The meeting in New Delhi was a late addition to the royal couple's India visit, which has also included their appearance at the annual Earthshot Prize
items.content:
The Prince and Princess of Wales have met with Prime Minister Narendra Modi to reflect on the enduring ties between the UK and India, as they wrapped up their three-day visit to the country.

William and Catherine arrived in New Delhi on Wednesday for the final leg of their first official overseas trip together in four years.

The meeting was a late addition to the couple's schedule and came after Modi confirmed he would be back from a scheduled trip to the Philippines in time to see the royals.

It comes a day after the royal couple were in Mumbai for the annual Earthshot Prize, which was founded by the prince and remains one of his biggest personal projects.

Street cricket with a legend then metro ride as William and Kate begin India visit

A Kensington Palace spokesperson said the royals and Modi discussed the "strength and importance of the UK–India bilateral relationship, reflecting on the deep and enduring ties between the two countries and the opportunities to strengthen their partnership in the years ahead".

The prince and princess also spoke "warmly" of their time in the country, thanking the prime minister and the people for their welcome, and added how much they enjoyed returning to India, a decade after their last visit.

Modi called it a "pleasure" to meet them, and said he looks forward to "further strengthening" the India-UK partnership for the "shared prosperity of the people of our nations and the wider world".

The couple last met the Indian prime minister on their official visit to India in 2016.

When Prince William announced earlier this year that The Earthshot Prize ceremony was going to be held in India for the first time, he highlighted India's leadership in climate innovation, its biodiversity and its massive youth population as the key reasons for choosing the country.

The royal spokesperson said that the meeting touched on the success of the ceremony in Mumbai, and India's "growing leadership in environmental innovation".

The event, founded by Prince William in 2020, was hosted this year by Karan Johar, presenter of The Traitors India and one of the country's most well-known film makers.

The first engagement of their visit saw them play street cricket in Mumbai alongside cricket star Sachin Tendulkar, who holds the record for being the highest run scorer in international cricket.

William and Catherine's first official overseas trip in four years was short, but allowed them to combine personal projects - like Earthshot - with diplomacy.

As the future king and queen, they are viewed as a valuable diplomatic asset by the UK government.

And with Catherine recovering well and back on international duties following her cancer treatment, visits of a similar kind can be expected to fill their calendar.

items.title: Lakegres: Vector search on existing Open/Hudi/Iceberg tables
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.onehouse.ai/blog/lakegres-vector-search-on-open-table-formats Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50549438 Points: 7 # Comments: 2
items.content:
Today we are announcing vector search in Onehouse Lakegres , with a native index stored inside existing and new open tables. You can search embeddings through a Postgres endpoint on the same tables you already have in your data lake. The index and data are managed in open formats in your own bucket.

A few years ago, adding vector search required a separate database. Postgres now has pgvector , OpenSearch has k-NN , and MySQL, Oracle, MongoDB and SQL Server have their own implementations. Databricks also offers vector search in Lakebase Search . Similarity search has become a standard index type for application data.

Most of the data an agent needs to query is in the lakehouse. Support transcripts, logs, documents, product catalogs and years of event history are stored in open tables on object storage. These datasets are 100 to 1,000 times larger than a typical Postgres instance. To search them with any of those databases, you have to copy the data into the database first. Copying lake-scale datasets into a relational database just to search their vectors is an absurd requirement. You end up paying to store the data twice and operating a pipeline to keep the copies in sync.

Yesterday, we announced unstructured data processing on Onehouse , which parses documents, images and video and stores their embeddings in open tables. Lakegres can now index and search those vectors, so agents can query that unstructured content alongside the business records already in the lakehouse.

Lakehouse and warehouse vendors have also added vector search. Each vendor below stores the index outside the open table, in a service or format that requires its own engine to read.

These vendors advocate open table formats while keeping their search indexes in closed formats. If you move to another engine, you have to rebuild every index in that vendor’s format, even though the underlying tables are open.

Most production vector search today runs on OpenSearch or Postgres. Both offer HNSW ( OpenSearch implementation , pgvector implementation ), a graph index that performs well when the entire graph fits in memory. AWS’s own sizing formula for OpenSearch is 1.1 × (4 × dimensions + 8 × m) bytes of RAM per vector. Our benchmark table has 247 million vectors at 1,024 dimensions. With m set to 16, that comes to about 1.15 TB of memory for one table, and about 46 TB at 10 billion vectors.

A pgvector HNSW index in Postgres also has to stay in shared buffers or the page cache to be fast, and latency degrades sharply once the working set exceeds RAM. Graph traversal is also a poor match for object storage, because each hop is a small random read . These designs work well for application databases with tens of millions of vectors. A data lake can be several orders of magnitude larger.

LinkedIn reported an exabyte across its Hadoop clusters in 2021. Uber’s lake holds 350 petabytes and ingests 6 trillion rows a day . Pinterest runs a 500-petabyte lake on Iceberg, and Netflix describes its Iceberg warehouse as exabyte scale . Embedding even a small fraction of these datasets produces billions of vectors. Keeping that many vectors in RAM is too expensive for most teams.

Training-data curation also needs large-scale similarity search. Post-training workflows can use it to select relevant examples and remove near-duplicates across large pools of candidate data. Repeated searches make cost per search matter as much as latency.

VAST , which supplies storage for AI training , uses a clustered vector index on flash in its distributed Element Store . Its launch material describes memory-resident indexes as prohibitively expensive at tens or hundreds of billions of vectors. turbopuffer also uses storage-based clustering. Lakegres applies this approach to existing Hudi and Iceberg tables through an open index.

Lakegres stores the vector index in the table’s metadata, in the same bucket as the data files. Commits that insert, update or delete rows also update the index. This keeps the index consistent with the table without a separate sync job or a second copy of the vectors. To our knowledge, this is the only available open vector search index for existing Hudi and Iceberg tables that is maintained with table writes and leaves the data files unchanged.

Iceberg support builds on the Hudi-backed indexing work in Apache XTable (Incubating) . We developed the design in the open with engineers from Uber and Walmart to support their planet-scale tables. The open RFC documents the storage layout, query path and consistency model.

The design is settled and ships in Lakegres today; the Hudi implementation is being upstreamed and XTable is in release-candidate testing ahead of OSS releases that other engines can integrate.

Lakegres accepts queries over the Postgres wire protocol, so any Postgres client or agent framework can run a similarity search in SQL. The same endpoint already serves analytical scans, indexed point lookups and text search on those tables.

The vector index is derived metadata . You can build it on an existing Hudi or Iceberg table with a vector column without rewriting the underlying data files. You can experiment with an index, rebuild it with different settings, or drop it when you no longer need it. Existing analytical queries continue to work. Trying vector search costs you an index build and its storage.

You do not have to move from Parquet to another file format like Lance or Vortex just to get vector search. Lakegres also already queries Lance and Vortex files while keeping the open table format the same. You can choose a file format for its storage and read characteristics independently of adding a vector index.

The base table stores the full vectors alongside the other columns. The index stores the smaller structures needed to find candidate rows: cluster centroids, quantizer state and packed index entries. These structures are stored in the table’s metadata and grouped into an index generation. Each query resolves a table snapshot and an active generation before reading the data, so it uses a compatible set of index structures throughout.

At build time, k-means groups vectors around representative points called centroids. Each vector is assigned to a cluster and encoded relative to its centroid using RaBitQ quantization. The encoding uses a fixed random rotation and compact codes at 1 to 8 bits per dimension, with 4 bits as the default. The stored codes support L2, cosine and dot-product distance calculations.

Clusters are divided into posting segments, with each segment stored in one metadata file group. Within a segment, roughly 1,000 to 4,000 vector entries are packed into a posting block, targeting about 512 KB. A posting contains the compressed scoring information, record key and a locator for the underlying row. Grouping them into blocks avoids creating billions of individual metadata records and lets the query read a cluster’s entries as contiguous key ranges.

Each block contains separate arrays for sign bits, extra precision bits, correction factors, row locators, dictionaries and record keys. The first scoring pass decodes the sign bits and factors. Later passes decode extra bits and row identities only for surviving candidates. The reader fetches the block as one record, then selectively decodes its arrays to reduce scoring work.

Lakegres first compares the query vector with the centroids and probes the nearest clusters. The nprobes setting controls how many clusters it opens. Probing more clusters generally improves recall at the cost of more work. Within those clusters, a first pass uses one-bit estimates and error bounds to discard candidates that cannot beat the current shortlist. A second pass uses the remaining bits to refine the surviving candidates.

Before returning results, the reader validates candidate keys against the record index at the query’s snapshot. Deleted candidates are removed and moved records are resolved to their current location. Approximate mode ranks the candidates with their compact codes. Optional exact re-ranking reads the shortlisted vectors from the base table and computes their full distances. Exact re-ranking improves the ordering within the candidate set. The search still examines only the selected clusters.

Each write adds small updates to the index. When a vector changes, the writer marks its old index entry as deleted and adds a new entry. When a row moves, the writer updates its location in the index. Queries read the packed blocks and these updates together. They use the latest entry for each record. Compaction periodically merges the updates into the blocks.

Before searching, the reader checks the table’s commit history. It verifies that the index includes the writes required by the query’s snapshot. A stale or incompatible index cannot serve the query. Depending on the configuration, the query either returns an error or scans the table for exact results.

You can rebuild the index while queries continue to run. The concurrency protocol coordinates table writes, index catch-up and snapshot reads so writers can keep committing while readers continue using a consistent index. The rebuild creates a new index version alongside the current one. It also picks up table writes made during the rebuild. Once the new version is ready, a single metadata commit makes it available to queries. Queries use the current version until the new version is online atomically. They never read a partially built index.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 is a masterpiece, say critics
items.summary: Critics have their say as to whether GTA 6, the most anticipated video game of all time, lives up to the hype.
items.content:
After 13 years of waiting, record-breaking trailers and lengthy delays, critics have given their answer to one of the year's biggest questions.

Does Grand Theft Auto 6, surely the most anticipated game of all time, live up to the hype?

Metacritic, which aggregates reviews from critics, averages it at 99 out of 100 , external - tying with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has held the record since 1998.

Reviewers overwhelmingly agreed the open-world action game was an ambitious, ground-breaking title that was well worth the wait.

Not everyone is enjoying the glowing praise - with some posters to online forums objecting to what one called "the ultra fan-boy hype."

But there is no question the reviewers have been effusive with their praise, with gaming website IGN , external branding GTA 6 "unprecedented", "unbelievable" and "unmissable".

Meanwhile in its five star review, Eurogamer said makers Rockstar had "pushed back the horizon of video games once again" with its graphics, storytelling and world building.

"The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome," reviewer Chris Tapsell wrote , external , but he added "there are also nits to pick".

For The New York Times , external one of those nits was whether the realism of the game might dull the fun chaos of its predecessors.

Reviewer Yussef Cole said GTA 6 had "matured beyond its memorable car crashes and stickups" with consequences to every action.

But "some of my favourite moments have been careening through streets with squad cars in hot pursuit," he wrote.

The graphics of the game were hotly anticipated and so far have not disappointed critics, with The Guardian , external describing Leonida, the setting inspired by Miami, as "so lifelike that at times it beggars belief".

And the relationship between the lead characters, Jason and Lucia, has also stunned critics.

"They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim," The Guardian's Keza MacDonald wrote, adding: "I found it impossible not to care for them".

Writing for Forbes , external , Paul Tassi said: "I can't say I've ever seen a better video game relationship than the one they share".

The Washington Post , external said GTA 6 "raises the bar at every level", while Bloomberg , external 's Jason Schreier called it a "masterpiece" in his five star review.

"It's hard not to be astonished by what Rockstar has done here," he wrote. "There's nothing else like it.

"While playing this game, I often found myself wondering how it even exists."

Rockstar hasn't revealed the cost of the game, but some estimates put the figure north of $1bn (£760m).

Gaming journalist Jordan Middler is one of the lucky few in the UK who got early access from Rockstar and tells BBC Newsbeat it is the "game of a generation".

He'd played for about 100 hours by the time he hit the credits and says he still has so much to do.

Middler did spot one negative though - he found the game can "slow down" because of how much is going on.

He also says it is "long overdue" that there is a female lead in Lucia.

"The way previous GTA games have dealt with women has been a boys' club approach," he says.

"Introducing Lucia and not making her some kind of token character, she just fits in completely... and she will quickly become a fan favourite without question."

The Game Awards - the most watched ceremony of its kind in the industry - gave players a teaser of the critical reception when its 2026 nominations were revealed on Tuesday.

And despite having not released at the time, GTA 6 was the most-nominated title.

It will be up for eight prizes, including game of the year and best music.

The nomination of Manni L Perez in the best performance category confirmed wide speculation that she is the actress behind main character Lucia in GTA 6 - a fact Rockstar hadn't previously officially confirmed.

The jury for the event is largely made up of gaming journalists around the world, who would have received advanced copies for review.

Some, though, have questioned how a game that has just been released has garnered such positive reviews and award nominations.

There is a view in some online forums that the hype around the game has got out of control as, with one poster commenting: "I think everyone's tired of hearing about this game - I don't even want to play it anymore."

It appears so far, however, that is likely to be very much a minority view.

items.title: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be US Speaker of the House
items.summary: The nomination sets him on the path to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber when Democrats take control of the House in January.
items.content:
Democrats in the US House of Representatives officially nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be Speaker, setting him on the path to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber.

The House will elect its new Speaker on 3 January, when the next term begins and Democrats will be in the majority.

His election to the powerful position - the Speaker is in line to succeed the president after the vice-president - is widely expected. Should he win, Jeffries will preside over his party's largest House majority in years and benefit from the partnership with a Senate also under Democrats' control.

Jeffries told reporters after the vote that the nomination was "a high honour and a distinct privilege".

As of Wednesday, Democrats will hold at least 257 seats in the House next year, with seven races still uncalled, which is well beyond the 218 needed for a majority.

Jeffries, who represents a district in New York, was re-elected as the party leader in a 251-11 closed-door vote on Wednesday. He has served as minority leader since 2023.

Despite overwhelming support in Wednesday's vote, Jeffries faced a handful of holdouts from new members in the party's left wing, who have said the party's sweeping victory in the midterm elections is a sign voters want change.

"While we have seen meaningful progress, there is still work to be done to ensure that the direction our party takes in this coming Congress reflects what our constituents are demanding of our leadership," seven incoming lawmakers, including fellow New Yorkers Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez, said in a statement.

All congressional Democrats are gearing up for clashes with the White House once they officially take control in January.

President Donald Trump, a Republican, has signalled a willingness to work with Democrats on some issues, but has also pledged to use his veto power to reject legislation he does not like.

That could make it hard for Democrats to deliver on their campaign promises to address affordability and pass other reforms.

At a news conference following the vote on Wednesday, Jeffries pledged House Democrats would "fight to lower the high costs of groceries and gas and housing", and "make healthcare affordable for every single American".

Though the party will have a large enough majority to weather defections on must-pass legislation, Jeffries will still have to navigate internal ideological divisions that have grown particularly sharp over US support of Israel and Americans' rising healthcare costs .

Many incoming Democrats, including members of the Democratic Socialists of America, won their elections by challenging the party establishment.

The Congressional Progressive Caucus, from the party's left wing, congratulated Jeffries on the nomination, adding they would "continue conversations with Leader Jeffries to ensure Democrats deliver a bold agenda for working people".

Along with shepherding legislation, Jeffries as Speaker will also have to manage the complex array of investigations that Democrats plan to launch into Trump, his family, and cabinet members now that they have regained control of the chamber's oversight powers.

Rounding out their party leadership team, House Democrats also elected Katherine Clark of Massachusetts as majority leader, Pete Aguilar of California as majority whip, and Joe Neguse of Colorado as assistant speaker.

items.title: 'Futuro Nazionale viola la legge Scelba', la Procura di Roma apre un fascicolo
items.summary: L'iniziativa segue un esposto presentato dal Sindacato dei militari per l'ipotesi di ricostituzione del partito fascista. Il legale dell'eurodeputato: 'Accuse inconsistenti anche per gli inquirenti'
items.content:
In seguito ad un esposto presentato dal Sindacato dei militari che adombrava la violazione della legge Scelba sulla ricostituzione del partito fascista da parte di Futuro Nazionale, il partito di Roberto Vannacci, la procura di Roma ha aperto un fascicolo modello 45, il registro degli atti non costituenti notizia di reato. Lo scrive Repubblica online. Nel documento presentato dal Sindacato, riporta il quotidiano, si chiede di verificare se Futuro Nazionale riproduca "il nucleo dottrinale antidemocratico e il metodo di lotta" del fascismo.

"Abbiamo, come sempre, piena fiducia nella magistratura. Apprendiamo con soddisfazione che la Procura di Roma ha iscritto l'esposto del Sindacato dei Militari a modello 45, il registro degli atti non costituenti notizia di reato. È quindi ragionevole supporre che, allo stato, le accuse appaiano inconsistenti anche agli inquirenti", afferma Giorgio Carta, legale dell'europarlamentare Roberto Vannacci.

"Non abbiamo ancora avuto modo di leggere l'esposto, tuttavia, per come sono state riportate dalla stampa, riteniamo le accuse del tutto infondate. Futuro Nazionale svolge la propria attività politica nel rispetto della Costituzione e delle regole democratiche. Respingiamo con fermezza ogni accusa e ogni eventuale ambizione di voler ricostituire il 'disciolto partito fascista', disciolto, appunto, più di 80 anni or sono" aggiunge spiegando che il "denunciante ha già presentato in passato esposti nei confronti del generale Vannacci, ma, per quanto ci consta, le contestazioni ivi formulate sono state tutte puntualmente archiviate".

Gli "accertamenti della Procura militare di Roma riguardano invece la posizione di singoli militari in servizio. Né il generale Vannacci né Futuro Nazionale risultano coinvolti in quegli accertamenti. Su quel fascicolo, quindi, non abbiamo osservazioni da formulare", conclude.

items.title: Allevamenti intensivi, l'85% degli italiani chiede un cambio di rotta
items.summary: Il sondaggio Youtrend per Essere Animali: 'Meno gabbie e più benessere animale'
items.content:
Gli italiani sempre più sensibili in materia di allevamenti intensivi, per i quali chiedono più tutele per il benessere degli animali e meno gabbie . E si dicono anche disponibili a spendere qualche euro in più, al momento di fare la spesa, per i cibi che nella produzione riducono le sofferenze degli animali. Un'attenzione, questa, che va al di là dei colori politici e appare piuttosto trasversale, visto che coinvolge elettori del centrodestra così come delle opposizioni.

E' quanto emerge da un sondaggio realizzato da Youtrend per Essere Animali e presentato alla Camera dei Deputati, secondo il quale il 31% degli italiani vorrebbe l’abolizione degli allevamenti intensivi, il 23% si augura la loro progressiva riduzione e un altro 31% li ritiene utili, ma pensa che andrebbero imposti standard più alti per il trattamento degli animali. Sommando questi dati si raggiunge un 85% di intervistati che chiedono cambiamenti in materia.

Per il 67% degli italiani il benessere animale dovrebbe costituire un criterio prioritario nell’assegnazione dei fondi pubblici agli allevamenti, criterio ancora più importante della qualità del prodotto e tutela dei lavoratori. E' di questa opinione il 64% degli elettori di Fratelli d’Italia, il 65% di quelli di Lega e Forza Italia, il 76% di chi vota Movimento 5 Stelle, il 79% dell’elettorato di Pd e Avs.

Il 63% degli intervistati è inoltre favorevole a vietare l'allevamento in gabbia delle galline per la produzione di uova, il 59% quello delle scrofe in gabbia durante la gestazione e l'allattamento, il 58% quello dei conigli in gabbia e il 52% l'allevamento dei vitelli in box individuali. Un tema, questo, al centro di una proposta di legge di iniziativa popolare promossa proprio da Essere Animali per l’abolizione delle gabbie negli allevamenti, che ha raccolto oltre 62.000 firme.

Dal sondaggio emerge inoltre che il 61% delle persone dice che spenderebbe di più per carne o pesce se avesse la certezza che sono stati prodotti riducendo al minimo la sofferenza degli animali. Il 44% sarebbe disposto a spendere fino al 50% in più su un prodotto da 10 euro al chilo, tipo il petto di pollo, il 12% arriverebbe a spendere il doppio, mentre il 5% spenderebbe anche il triplo. Inoltre, il metodo di allevamento è una fortissima leva per le scelte di acquisto, seconda solo al Paese di provenienza, ma più decisiva rispetto al marchio o alle certificazioni IGP e DOP.

Per Eleonora Evi, deputato del Partito democratico, "la tutela della natura e degli animali non è un tema di nicchia, ma una richiesta che cresce nella società, e la politica ha il dovere di ascoltarla". "Da tempo chiediamo al Governo di farsi sentire a Bruxelles perché la Commissione mantenga gli impegni sul benessere animale, a partire dalla fine delle gabbie chiesta da oltre un milione di cittadini europei", sottolinea Dolores Bevilacqua, senatrice del M5S, promotrice anche di una mozione in materia. Secondo Walter Rizzetto, deputato di Fratelli d’Italia, "la sfida dei prossimi anni sarà proprio quella di costruire un equilibrio tra tutela degli animali, sostenibilità ambientale, qualità delle produzioni e tenuta economica delle aziende agricole".

items.title: Atp Finals: Alcaraz rassicura, piccolo fastidio che non preoccupa
items.summary: Lo spagnolo: 'Ho mantenuto la calma e gestito la situazione in campo'
items.content:
"Mi sentivo a mio agio, molto sicuro, ma all'improvviso è sorto un piccolo problema: ho avvertito una sensazione a livello dell'ischio. Fortunatamente avevo già un break di vantaggio, il che mi ha permesso di mantenere la calma e di gestire la situazione. Ho semplicemente cercato di restare calmo e concentrato per continuare a esprimere un buon tennis. Non è una cosa che mi preoccupa più di tanto". A dirlo, nella conferenza stampa post partita alle Atp Finals, è Carlos Alcaraz, rassicurando sulle sue condizioni fisiche dopo la vittoria su Daniil Medvedev alle ATp Finals. "Ho fiducia nel mio team e ho davanti a me un giorno e mezzo che sarà importante - aggiunge -. Staremo a vedere, ma credo davvero di poter giocare a un buon livello".

"Dopo l'intervento del fisioterapista ho cercato di restare rilassato e di continuare a giocare in modo composto, evitando movimenti azzardati - spiega ancora Alcaraz -. Soprattutto, mi sono concentrato sul mantenere la calma. Credo di aver giocato con gran lucidità da quel momento in poi, restando molto concentrato, in particolare sui colpi e nei game in risposta, dove ho cercato di essere il più aggressivo possibile. Ho puntato a seguire il piano di gioco che stavo già attuando, mantenendo alta l'attenzione sul servizio. Avere un break di vantaggio è stato fondamentale per poter continuare a giocare secondo il mio stile - conclude -. Non è cambiato granché, se non per la necessità di una maggiore cautela, specialmente in fase difensiva, ma per il resto è rimasto tutto uguale".

items.content:
Hi HN, we're Ary and Maria, co-founders of Maritime (https://maritime.sh). We're building an agent-native cloud that handles everything from custom environments to lifecycle management for AI agents.

Demo: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lCWMdBQ96rY

There’s been an explosion of sandbox companies coming out of SF, but sandboxes solve maybe 10% of the infrastructure problem for AI agents. The approach that most sandboxing companies take is:

You buy Hetzner/OVH Cloud bare metal servers, use Firecracker to slice the servers up into VMs, sell those VMs with low margins.

It’s a bit of an oversimplification, but the point is it’s a narrow solution to a fairly difficult problem.

We talked to a couple hundred companies that are building AI agents. From personal assistants and coding agents to specialized healthcare agents, and the main pattern we saw was that even after choosing a sandbox provider, you still have to build additional infrastructure just to get things working. These were the primary points of friction:

1. Agent lifecycle management.

There’s a lot that you have to build in order to properly give your agents VMs: things like sleep/wake, persistent storage, triggers, scheduling, per-user routing and spend caps, health monitoring, failure recovery, and deploying updates across thousands of VMs without downtime. There are so many of these small sandbox management tasks that companies have to build and maintain themselves, and they add up.

2. Custom environments.

Production agents have varying needs. Some agents need Windows applications. Others need Android, browsers with persistent sessions, custom operating system images, preinstalled desktop software and applications, or specific dependencies. Some agents need access to private networks to interact with customer-specific things on prem, or residential IPs, or the ability to restrict network access completely.

3. Cost optimization.

If you’re selling a personal assistant for $20/month, a sandbox that costs $0.04/hour comes out to roughly $29/month if you keep it running continuously, not including LLM inference, storage, etc. There is a way to combat this though, which is to optimize sandbox usage with auto-snapshotting, making things event-driven, mounting S3 buckets to agent environments via FUSE for cheap storage, cold-tiering snapshots, etc. All roads lead to… building more infrastructure.

So what did we build differently?

We give each agent its own isolated, persistent microVM and a configurable environment. On top of the compute, we built a lot of composable services: provisioning, persistent state, sleep/wake orchestration, triggers, schedule creation, monitoring, network configuration, updates, rollbacks, recovery, per-agent spend tracking, login handoffs, all the things you’d need for production agents.

We also spent a huge amount of time optimizing cost. A lot of thought was put into things such as scale-to-zero, copy-on-write over shared base images, compressed memory snapshots, hot/warm/cold snapshot and disk tiering, and other optimizations while balancing these with performance metrics like latency.

As a result, Maritime costs $1 for a 2gb RAM agent per month (unlimited usage for that $1), with additional resources available as needed.

Maria was a visiting lecturer at MIT and did research at Project NANDA on agent infrastructure. Ary did research on agent coordination protocols at the same lab. We started Maritime together this March because of all the issues we faced with trying to deploy agents to the cloud during our research.

We want your feedback.

If you're building an agent product, what did you have to build on top of sandboxes to make them work? We want to know about all the workarounds and weird things you’ve had to build.

Are there things you’ve tried to build with VMs but couldn’t? Does Maritime fit your needs? Is there a feature we’re missing that would make us more enticing?

Happy to answer any questions in the comments.

items.title: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia
items.summary: Watch: The BBC's Jonathan Beale joins Ukrainian forces taking the battle below ground and out of sight of Russian drones.
items.content:
For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the Kharkiv region.

The BBC is the first international broadcaster to enter the pipeline where this subterranean battle is taking place.

With a diameter of just over a metre there's enough room only to crawl. But it is relatively safe from the drones that now saturate the skies above the front line – and which are making it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance.

The BBC's defence correspondent Jonathan Beale reports from near Kupyansk, where he went underground with the 13th Khartiia Operational Brigade.

items.title: 'The drones don't fly here' - BBC reports from Ukraine's new front line
items.summary: Ukrainian forces are fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet tunnel in the Kharkiv region.
items.content:
There's a new front in the war in Ukraine, and it is underground.

For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the north-eastern Kharkiv region.

With a diameter of just over a metre there is enough room only to crawl. But it is relatively safe from the drones that now saturate the skies above the front line – and make it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance.

Going underground is now the "only option", says Zanuda, who has helped plan Ukraine's tunnel operation and calls it a new world of fighting. But, he acknowledges, it is hard.

"On the surface you always have some room to manoeuvre, but here you can only engage the enemy head-on."

The journey to get to this subterranean battleground in the Kharkiv region only reinforced the dangers on the ground: a high-speed move by vehicle across open fields, followed by a long march across muddy ground – accompanied by Ukrainian troops with their weapons loaded, ready to shoot down Russian drones.

Arriving at the tunnel entrance, the first thing to hit you is the lingering smell of gas and fetid air.

Both sides use openings in the pipeline to get to the surface, where most of the fighting takes place. They have made breaches in the ground, and used welding tools to break through the thick steel.

The Russians were the first to exploit the pipe to infiltrate the nearby city of Kupyansk in September 2025. They have used underground pipelines before, during the capture of the city of Avdiivka in 2024, and last year in their bid to recapture areas of Russia's Kursk region.

A specially designed electric cart transports troops and supplies through the pipeline.

They call it the Kupyansk metro. It occasionally breaks down. We travelled on it for 40 minutes, heads bowed and legs crossed. There is a regular bump as you cross the welded sections of the pipe. It is like an austere fairground ride, without the fun.

Our destination was a break in the pipeline where Ukrainian troops have built dug-outs to store ammunition and equipment, with just enough room to stand. It is where the man they call Musician conducts the movement of troops and supplies. He has been living like a mole, his face engrained with dirt and earth.

Musician tells me he has spent the past three months there, with a few brief visits above ground to clean up or go to the toilet. From time to time we can hear the thuds of artillery rounds above. Musician tells me we are close to the line of contact: "But it's safe underground."

The cart continues its journey into the bowels of the earth. It returns about half an hour later with more troops covered in dirt. They have been fighting in positions on the surface.

"It's more comfortable in the pipe because drones don't fly here, and neither do artillery shells or glide bombs," says Vovochka, who has been fighting on the ground for the past three weeks.

But there has been fighting in the pipeline, too. Operation Veles, named after a mythical Slavic god of the underworld, began in April. Since then Ukraine has advanced 15km (9.3 miles) along the pipeline.

It has been painstaking, backbreaking work – with the ever-present fear of coming into contact with the enemy.

Back above ground we meet a few of the soldiers, from the 13th Khartiia Brigade of Ukraine's National Guard, who have taken part in the mission. Their first task was to clear the detritus, water and Russian barricades inside the pipeline.

The Ukrainian troops say some of the barriers were boobytrapped or piled with Russian bodies. "When we moved them or climbed over them, we had no idea what was underneath," says Chyzh.

The other danger, he said, was the ricochets from gunfire when they tried to advance. "You never know where a bullet is going to go or how it will bounce."

His comrade Kort says "we were all firing, we were pushing them back". Over the course of the operation Ukraine says it killed more than 100 Russian soldiers and took 30 prisoners. "Yes, there were bodies," says Kort. "I even had to sleep right next to them."

Their commander's former life as a miner helped prepare them for the physical and psychological challenges of operating underground.

From a building on the surface, Biashym keeps in regular contact with his men still in the pipeline. Behind him is a cabinet full of medicine.

Soldiers in the pipeline spend much of their time on their knees and suffer abrasions. Biashym admits some have had panic attacks from living in such a confined space. Others have struggled to breathe.

Hundreds of Colombian volunteers have also been involved in the operation, part of the RUG 23rd Assault Regiment.

Foreign fighters have helped boost Ukraine's depleted ranks. One of the Colombians, whose call sign is Gecko, tells me it took them 30 days to just clear 500m.

"It was difficult, it was hot and I had fear inside the pipe," he said. "But at some point I just thought, OK, just deal with it and let's advance."

Russian forces, like Ukraine's, have built fortified positions inside the pipeline. They still try to infiltrate Ukrainian positions, burrowing their way in and out of the pipe. From a control room above ground we watched Ukrainian drones target another Russian attempt to outflank them.

While some of the fighting taking place underground, there are still battles on the surface and in the air. It has been a combined operation.

But, Zanuda believes it is the best way to fight in the future. "Ground operations are now nearly impossible," he said, adding that "everyone understands, for now, the only way to fight is underground".

There'll be more missions like this, he believes. "Pipelines run everywhere," he said. "You have to remember, back in the Soviet times, oil, gas and ammonia were being transported to Europe, with the entire transit route running through Ukraine."

In reality it has been brutal, gruelling and dangerous work in the harshest of conditions.

It has taken Ukraine seven months to clear 15km of the pipeline.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has hailed it as a success.

It has helped retake lost territory and been a boost for morale, but on its own it has not changed the course of the war.

Additional reporting by Moose Campbell, Volodymyr Lozhko and Rebecca Hartmann

items.title: Londra, donna divorzia da un amico di Putin e chiede 720 milioni per “ragionevoli necessità”
items.summary: Inizia il processo di Natalia Potanina contro l’ex marito Vladimir Potanin, oligarca russo e compagno di hockey del presidente Vladimir Putin. La donna potrebbe ottenere l’assegno più ricco della storia della capitale britannica
items.content:
LONDRA - Almeno 600 milioni di sterline, ossia 720 milioni di euro, che Natalia Potanina giudica come “ragionevole necessita”, per quello che potrebbe diventare il più ricco assegno di divorzio nella storia inglese . Oggi, all’Alta Corte di Londra, è iniziato il processo che vede la donna contro un oligarca russo , nonché suo ex marito e molto vicino a Putin, Vladimir Potanin.

I due si sono sposati nel 1983, per poi divorziare dodici anni fa in Russia. Ma nel frattempo, Potanina si è trasferita a Londra, ha ricevuto la cittadinanza britannica e punta ad ottenere nei tribunali inglesi un risarcimento mostruoso che l’ex moglie considera necessario per coprire le spese di 150 milioni per una nuova casa a Londra, la bellezza di 441 milioni per il “mantenimento" e altri 10 milioni per ulteriori spese patrimoniali. Eppure, come racconta il Telegraph , la vita di Vladimir e Natalia, entrambi 65enni, sembrava una favola: "Nel 1983, dopo essersi conosciuti tra i banchi di una scuola superiore di Mosca, si sposano. Come molti nella Russia dell’epoca sovietica, non possiedono praticamente nulla. In quei primi anni di difficoltà, ha ricordato Potanina, vivono praticamente senza un soldo nell’appartamento dei genitori di lei". Ma poi arrivano gli anni Novanta, "le industrie vengono privatizzate e Potanin, che negli anni è diventato il “compagno di partite di hockey” del presidente Putin, diviene uno degli oligarchi più ricchi della Russia: un magnate dei metalli che ancora oggi figura al 79esimo posto nella classifica degli uomini più ricchi del mondo ”.

Fino al divorzio in Russia, nel 2014, dal quale Potanina avrebbe già ottenuto tra i 30 e i 60 milioni di sterline. Ma non bastano alla donna, anche per il suo tenore di vita a Londra, anche se anni fa a una giornalista dichiarò: “Il denaro non ha alcun valore intrinseco per me”. Il processo dovrebbe durare due settimane. Gli avvocati di Potanina chiedono innanzitutto che le venga riconosciuta una ampia quota del patrimonio dell’ex marito che, secondo le loro stime, è raddoppiato dal 2018, raggiungendo i 29,7 miliardi di dollari (22,5 miliardi di sterline). Secondo il diritto inglese, Potanina non ha diritto a ricevere per sempre il 50% del reddito dell'ex marito, ma potrebbe arrivarci vicino. Qualora questa richiesta venisse respinta, Potanina chiederà comunque almeno 600 milioni di sterline per coprire le sue "ragionevoli necessità”, di cui abbiamo parlato sopra. "Se dovesse vincere”, nota il quotidiano conservatore, "la somma che le verrebbe riconosciuta potrebbe superare il record di 554 milioni di sterline stabilito dall'Alta Corte di Londra nel 2021, dopo il divorzio tra il sovrano di Dubai, lo sceicco Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum , e la principessa Haya bint Al Hussein”.

Come nota il Times , nel 1995 Potanin ha acquisito una partecipazione in Norilsk Nickel, un colosso metallurgico di cui oggi possiede oltre un terzo del capitale. L’oligarca, che in passato ha spesso giocato a hockey su ghiaccio insieme al presidente russo, "è stato anche cofondatore di Onexim Bank e in passato ha avuto interessi nei settori assicurativo, dei media, dell’agricoltura e del petrolio. Detiene partecipazioni nella società farmaceutica Petrovax e nella stazione sciistica di Rosa Khutor, vicino a Sochi, e possiede uffici e alberghi a Mosca”.

items.title: DLSS 4.5 arriva in EVE Vanguard, Teardown e Blender 5.3
items.summary: Lalpha di EVE Vanguard debutta con DLSS 4.5 e Blender 5.3 lo usa per le anteprime 3D.
items.content:
NVIDIA ha esteso il supporto al DLSS 4.5 all'alpha di EVE Vanguard e a giochi già disponibili come Teardown e Lightyear Frontierm ma vale la pena dire che l'aggiornamento più insolito riguarda Blender 5.3, dove la stessa famiglia di tecnologie aiuta a ripulire l'anteprima delle scene 3D mentre si lavora su luci, materiali e inquadrature.

In Blender la novità si chiama Ray Reconstruction. Ma cosa comporta? Una scena illuminata con il ray tracing può apparire granulosa durante i primi istanti del calcolo, quando il programma ha ancora raccolto pochi campioni di luce per ogni pixel, e la ricostruzione serve a ridurre quel rumore nel viewport, cioè nella finestra in cui si modifica la scena.

Si può così giudicare prima come cade una luce o come si riflette su una superficie, senza aspettare ogni volta un render completo, e la versione 5.3 introduce anche il supporto nativo ai dispositivi RTX Spark.

items.title: A Genova la cerimonia d'apertura di Best, il summit dell'economia del mare
items.summary: Vago, la blue economy non è settore ma un modello per il futuro
items.content: È stato inaugurato a Genova, nel Padiglione Blu – Jean Nouvel al Waterfront di Levante, BEST – The Blue Economy Summit & Trade Show, il primo summit biennale internazionale dedicato all’economia del mare. L’evento, promosso da Blue Media - società del Gruppo MSC attiva nei settori dei media, dell’editoria e degli eventi - è in programma fino a giovedì 19 novembre. La cerimonia di apertura e il taglio del nastro sono state condotte dal direttore del Secolo XIX Andrea Castanini. Nella sala plenaria sono intervenuti il presidente di Assarmatori Stefano Messina, il presidente di Confitarma Mario Zanetti, il segretario generale di Confcommercio Marco Barbieri, il vicepresidente di Confindustria Antonio Gozzi, il presidente esecutivo di Rina Ugo Salerno e l’amministratore delegato di Axpo Italia Simone Demarchi. Presenti anche il presidente di Regione Liguria Marco Bucci, la sindaca di Genova Silvia Salis, il presidente della Camera di Commercio di Genova Luigi Attanasio e il presidente dell’Autorità di Sistema Portuale del Mar Ligure Occidentale Matteo Paroli. “Oggi - ha commentato dal palco il presidente di Blue Media Pierfrancesco Vago - stiamo lanciando una nuova piattaforma collettiva perché la blue economy non è solo un settore della nostra economia, ma un modello per il nostro futuro. L’Europa ha strutturalmente bisogno di valorizzare in maniera più incisiva gli asset dell'economia del mare per rafforzare la propria competitività globale. BEST vuole essere il primo tassello di una visione lungimirante, uno strumento per favorire una maggiore cooperazione tra i diversi soggetti del sistema industria della blue economy”. Dopo la cerimonia è stata inaugurata la mostra ‘Mediterraneo, il mare, il lavoro, l’uomo’ di Giuseppe Rivaroli, a cura di Federlogistica. BEST si svilupperà nell'arco di quattro giornate, con un programma congressuale di oltre 30 sessioni di confronto tra armatori, operatori portuali e logistici, rappresentanti delle istituzioni e di centri di ricerca, dell’industria, energia, finanza. In parallelo, un’area espositiva di 20mila metri quadrati. L’obiettivo della manifestazione è favorire il dialogo tra i diversi comparti dell’economia del mare e creare nuove opportunità di business, valorizzando il contributo dell’innovazione e delle competenze. I contenuti sono organizzati attorno a tre macroaree – Shipping, porti e logistica; Turismo costiero e marittimo; Fattori trasversali – e seguono un percorso che dallo scenario internazionale arriva alle condizioni necessarie per la crescita del settore.

items.summary: Lassistente di Proton arriva su computer con connettori, pianificazioni e istruzioni riutilizzabili.
items.content:
Lumo si può ora installare su Windows, macOS e Linux, questa è la novità per l'assistente di Proton. Ora che è disponibile anche su desktop, introduce tre novità che cambiano il modo in cui lo si usa. La prima è che può cercare informazioni nei file e nelle app collegate, la seconda che può svolgere attività a un orario stabilito, e la terza è che è in grado di riutilizzare istruzioni salvate in precedenza.

La differenza si vede quando la risposta dipende da qualcosa che si trova già sul computer. Per rintracciare un documento si può chiedere a Lumo di cercarlo nelle cartelle a cui gli è stato dato accesso. Tra le integrazioni ci sono Google Drive, Jira e Confluence, mentre per collegare Proton Mail serve Proton Mail Bridge. L'app supporta anche server MCP locali o remoti, con cui si possono aggiungere altri strumenti.

Per ogni connettore si può decidere cosa lasciar fare all'assistente, e ad esempio una configurazione possibile è permettergli di cercare nella posta, chiedere un'approvazione ogni volta che deve inviare un messaggio e bloccare del tutto le cancellazioni. La distinzione conta soprattutto quando una richiesta passa dalla lettura di un documento a un'azione che modifica qualcosa.

items.title: Julio Iglesias facing court investigation over alleged sexual offences
items.summary: The 83-year-old singer is accused of abusing two former employees at Caribbean residences in 2021.
items.content:
Singer Julio Iglesias is facing an investigation by Spain's national court over allegations he sexually abused and assaulted two female former staff members

Two women, who worked for the 83-year-old in the Caribbean, have accused him of abuse which they say took place in the Bahamas and the Dominican Republic in 2021.

The announcement comes after Spanish prosecutors dropped an inquiry into the claims earlier this year after concluding that they lacked jurisdiction because the alleged crimes took place abroad.

Iglesias, who has been a household name in Spain since the 1960s and has sold millions of records worldwide, has previously denied the allegations .

But in a statement published on Wednesday , external (in Spanish), national court Judge Antonio Piña said the account given in the complaint, alongside preliminary evidence provided, justified opening criminal proceedings.

He added that the investigation would cover parts of the complaint relating to potential crimes against sexual freedom, as well as assault and degrading treatment.

But the court will not investigate claims made in the lawsuit of human trafficking or crimes against workers' rights. Piña said these allegations were dismissed after the he looked into the hiring of the women and found there was "no deception or artifice involved".

Piña said the former employees had been summoned to testify in person on 3 February.

The announcement comes after Spain's public prosecutor's office shifted its position last month, saying it now believed the court had jurisdiction to investigate the allegations.

In its statement, the national court said Spanish law sets out that courts can hear cases of crimes committed abroad by Spanish citizens provided certain conditions are met.

The allegations against Iglesias first emerged in a joint three-year investigation between Spanish newspaper El Diario , external and television network Univision news, published in January.

In that investigation, the two women were identified as a domestic worker and a physical therapist, who described alleged sexual abuse and degrading working conditions.

The domestic worker, whose name was changed to Rebeca in the reports, said Iglesias would regularly call her to his room at the end of the day and would touch her inappropriately without consent.

Rebeca, a Dominican who was 22 when the alleged events took place, also alleged that Iglesias had forced her to take part in threesomes with another female member of staff. She also described the singer slapping her in the face and grabbing her genitals.

The other woman, a Venezuelan physical therapist named as Laura in the article, said Iglesias had touched her breasts and kissed her on the mouth against her will. She added that he constantly threatened to fire her, controlled how much food she ate and asked her about when her period was due.

Rebeca and Laura filed an initial legal complaint in January against Iglesias for sexual assault and human trafficking.

In a response to the allegations in January, Iglesias said , external : "I deny having abused, coerced, or disrespected any woman. These accusations are absolutely false and deeply sadden me."

On Wednesday, the court said the lawsuit had been accepted based on evidence provided in the complaint. This included a photograph of one of the complainants, showing a bruise on her arm that was "consistent with the possibility of her being grabbed forcefully".

It added that the same photo showed "two marks on one of her thighs that could correspond to a human bite", which the complainant said were "a consequence of her forced participation in acts of a sexual nature".

WhatsApp message exchanges, including New Year's greetings, which suggest an "affectionate" relationship between the women and Iglesias, will also be considered, the court said.

But it added that the seemingly cordial tone, which presents "an apparent discrepancy with certain aspects of the narrative", would be clarified through a "complete and contextualised examination of the communications".

The claim over violations of workers' rights could not be investigated because there is no comparable criminal offence in the Bahamas and the Dominican Republic, where the alleged crimes took place, it said.

Iglesias is one of the most successful Latin artists of all time, having sold more than 300 million records in a career spanning decades.

He is also the father of fellow music superstar Enrique Iglesias.

La differenza di 1.500 euro, dunque, è legata alla formula creditizia e non costituisce uno sconto incondizionato. Naturalmente, è sempre doveroso verificare tutte le condizioni del contratto (visibili anche sul sito di Fiat).Per ottenere il prezzo più basso è necessario immatricolare l'auto entro il 26 novembre 2026. La disponibilità di esemplari in pronta consegna può facilitare il rispetto della scadenza, ma va verificata direttamente con la concessionaria.

Rate da 149 euro oppure finanziamento a interessi zero

La proposta da 17.950 euro prevede un anticipo di 5.281 euro, seguito da 35 rate mensili da 149 euro e da una rata finale di 11.837,20 euro. Il TAN fisso è dell'8,99% e il TAEG del 12,27%. Quest'ultimo dato rende evidente perché il prezzo promozionale non debba essere confuso con il costo complessivo dell'operazione.Chi preferisce evitare gli interessi può valutare l'alternativa con TAN zero. In questo caso il prezzo della 600 Pop è di 20.450 euro, con anticipo di 4.368 euro, 35 rate da 149 euro e rata finale di 11.837,20 euro. Il TAEG è comunque del 2,11%, perché restano le spese accessorie.Entrambe le offerte sono rivolte ai privati, soggette all'approvazione finanziaria e non cumulabili con altre iniziative. Alla scadenza, se si restituisce o sostituisce l'auto, è previsto un addebito di 0,10 euro per ogni chilometro oltre i 30.000 contrattuali.

Porte aperte, disponibili anche Hybrid ed elettrica

Il porte aperte permette anche di confrontare le altre anime della Fiat 600. Accanto alla Turbo 100 trova posto la 600 Hybrid, con sistema elettrificato a 48 volt e cambio automatico a doppia frizione, pensata per chi desidera una guida più fluida nel traffico senza collegare l'auto a una presa.La 600e è invece completamente elettrica e si rivolge a chi può organizzare le ricariche in funzione dei propri spostamenti. Per tutte e tre le versioni, la rete Fiat propone la possibilità di vedere gli allestimenti disponibili e prenotare una prova su strada.[drivek_widget brand_id="fiat" model_id="grande-panda-benzina"]

items.title: Sharp AQUOS sense11 pesa 157 g e ha un OLED da 3.000 nit
items.summary: Sharp presenta un medio gamma da 157 g con batteria da 5.000 mAh e sei anni di patch.
items.content:
Sharp ha presentato il nuovo AQUOS sense11, uno smartphone Android dal peso 157 grammi, che racchiude una batteria da 5.000 mAh in una scocca di alluminio spessa 7,6 mm. Sharp si sbilancia positivamente e stima due giorni di autonomia con un profilo che prevede dieci ore di utilizzo al giorno, quattro delle quali in streaming video.

Per quanto riguarda il display da 6,2 pollici, la luminosità di picco arriva a 3.000 nit, ma la scheda tecnica riporta anche il dato con lo schermo interamente bianco, pari a 1.500 nit. Sharp indica una frequenza variabile da 1 Hz fino a 240 Hz equivalenti. Il valore più alto si ottiene in alcune app inserendo un fotogramma nero tra gli aggiornamenti effettivi, che arrivano a 120 al secondo. L'inserimento riduce la sfocatura percepita quando qualcosa si muove rapidamente sullo schermo.

Il processore è lo Snapdragon 7s Gen 3 e la RAM del modello base arriva a 8 GB, ma chi usa la microSD per foto e video può aggiungere fino a 2 TB anche alla versione da 128 GB. Sul fronte software si parte da Android 17, con un massimo di quattro aggiornamenti di versione e sei anni di patch di sicurezza dal lancio.

items.title: Trump shakes hands with Putin and Xi ahead of historic talks in China
items.summary: The three leaders will meet together for the first time on Thursday during a closely-watched summit.
items.content:
Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met for the first time in more than a year on Wednesday, as they prepared for landmark talks in China with Xi Jinping.

The US president was greeted off his plane by the Chinese leader as he arrived in Shenzhen for a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders, which will culminate in a closely-watched meeting between the pair and the Russian president.

After a carefully choreographed handshake and hug between Trump and Xi on the tarmac, the US president later greeted and exchanged pleasantries with Putin ahead of a reception.

Trump and Putin are expected to hold one-on-one talks on the sidelines of the summit on Thursday, in which the war in Ukraine could be discussed.

However the main focus during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum (Apec) will be on the US-China-Russia talks on Thursday - the first time the trio of leaders have met together in person.

A full agenda has not been made public but there have been various hints about what could be discussed, including the wars in Ukraine and Iran, nuclear proliferation, trade tensions and developments in artificial intelligence.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Putin and Trump have not yet held a substantive meeting, and merely greeted each other on Wednesday.

Peskov also said that "no more than an hour" had been allocated for Thursday's trilateral talks between Putin, Trump and Xi.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has raised fears of a plan to end the war being discussed in the absence of representatives from Kyiv or Europe.

It is unclear whether China would want this issue to be on the agenda in Shenzhen, with Beijing talking more generally about the need to discuss "safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability".

China has officially remained neutral since Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, rejecting accusations from Kyiv and its allies that it has been tacitly supporting Moscow, including by exporting dual-use technology used by the Russian military.

Wednesday's handshake was the first in-person meeting between Trump and Putin since August 2025, when the Russian leader travelled to Alaska for talks on the Ukraine war which failed to deliver a breakthrough.

Xi's personal reception for Trump at the airport mimicked a similar move by the US president when the Chinese leader visited Washington in September, a gesture Xi described as "special".

In Shenzhen, a red carpet was rolled out in front of Air Force One for Trump, with a cheering crowd, honour guard, military flyover and flowers presentation all in place to welcome him.

Chinese state-run news agency Xinhua quoted Xi as saying he wanted to pursue a "constructive strategic and stable relationship based on respect, fairness, and equality".

Xi's greeting will be seen as a diplomatic gesture designed to begin the week's talks with his American counterpart on a cordial note.

The south-east Chinese city the Apec summit is being held in is a booming area for manufacturing and advanced tech.

It comes against the backdrop of the ousting of Nvidia chief executing Jensen Huang, who admitted to having an affair with a woman suspected by US intelligence of spying for Beijing - a claim dismissed as a "smear" by China.

Trump has pursued warmer relations with China but the incident points to ongoing tensions between the two powers.

Several hours before Trump's arrival, Putin landed in Shenzhen and held around two hours of talks with Xi, with whom he has pressed for closer economic and defence relations.

Xi said both countries would "move forward steadily and boldly" and that the relationship was "stable as a mountain, unshaken by storms".

items.title: YouTube Music, sparisce la scheda Samples: dove ritrovarla
items.summary: YouTube Music semplifica la barra su Android e iOS. Le anteprime restano nellapp.
items.content:
YouTube Music sta per introdurre una novità nell'interfaccia, togliendo la scheda Samples dalla barra in basso su Android e iOS. I video verticali con cui il servizio fa scoprire brani e artisti restano nell'app, ma per aprirli bisognerà partire dalla pagina di un artista, di un album o di una playlist, e il pulsante si troverà in alto a destra. A dire il vero la barra cambia aspetto a seconda dell'abbonamento, perché chi usa Premium vedrà tre voci, Home, Cerca e Raccolta, mentre nella versione gratuita rimarrà anche una quarta scheda per passare al piano a pagamento.

Secondo 9to5Google, la modifica verrà attivata lato server, ma in realtà è già in distribuzione da alcune settimane. Se qualcuno se lo stesse chiedendo, il fatto che il tasto sia ancora visibile su un proprio telefono è compatibile con una distribuzione di tipo graduale, pertanto potrebbe essere solamente questione di giorni.

Quando YouTube ha introdotto Samples, nel 2023, l'idea era di offrire un feed musicale da scorrere come gli Shorts, e si poteva aprire direttamente dalla schermata iniziale e passare in pochi secondi dall'ultima uscita di un artista emergente a un brano meno conosciuto di un nome già affermato, ma ora il punto di partenza è più specifico.

items.title: Microsoft AI: Seven new world-class models at scalable price-performance
items.summary: Article URL: https://microsoft.ai/news/microsoft-ignite-2026/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50548021 Points: 140 # Comments: 89
items.content:
At MAI, our mission is to build you the very best models in the world and keep every developer and every enterprise at the frontier of capability.

But as token spend skyrockets, we know that you also want models at a price point that lets you run agents 24-7 doing real engineering work.

That’s why today we’re releasing a family of seven new world class models at a truly exceptional price-performance:

Security, alignment and containment are the most important priorities for agent development in 2027 and beyond. That’s our top priority. We need to run monitoring and control agents defending and patching live production systems 24-7. That’s why MAI Cyber 2 Flash was designed to deliver frontier intelligence at a fraction of the cost.

Built with Microsoft’s decades of proprietary data and world class security expertise, our models help defenders stay safe in this new era where attackers have cheap and abundant offensive tools.

MAI Cyber 2 Flash builds on earlier MAI Cyber models that defenders already rely on. MAI Cyber accounts for almost 40% of scans in MDASH, and 90% of scans that started with MAI continued to use it. Our latest model is now priced 86% lower on output tokens than MAI Cyber 1.1 Flash, giving existing MDASH customers a stronger model at a lower price.

MAI Code 2 is built for the best price-performance for everyday enterprise coding tasks. Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot (DeepSWE 1.1, Terminal Bench 2.1, SWE-Atlas and FrontierCode v1.1), MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT-6.1 Sol at 40% of the price, and 96% of Claude Opus 5.5’s performance at just 5% of the price.

We’ve built these models to prioritize the coding work our customers do every day. They’re explicitly not yet tuned for harder problems, like fundamental science research and very long horizon agentic work.

MAI Code 2 also been tuned to generate great dashboards and visualizations. In a blind, side-by-side evaluation of frontend work, developers preferred MAI Code 2 over GPT-6 Sol 64% of the time. Try MAI Code 2 in GitHub Copilot today. Read more here .

MAI Code 2 Flash is designed for high-volume, everyday tasks like code explanations, targeted edits, routine fixes, and rapid iterations, while bringing quality at a much lower cost. It performs comparably to GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 at 65% and 20% of the price, respectively, across three coding benchmarks measuring day-to-day, high-volume routine coding tasks (DeepSWE 1.1, Terminal Bench 2.1 and SWE-Atlas). It’s available in GitHub Copilot and in a limited-access preview in Microsoft Foundry .

MAI Image 2.7 is the best image editing model in the world, taking the #1 spot on Artificial Analysis, outperforming GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst (max) at just one-fifth of the price. At text-to-image generation, our model is ranked #4, making us the second-best lab. And MAI Image 2.7 Flash brings world class image generation for high-volume scenarios at ~$10 per 1,000 images. Both are available in Microsoft Foundry here .

MAI Realtime 1 is our first live speech-to-speech model, designed for natural, low-latency conversations. In our evaluations, it outperformed GPT-Realtime 2.1 across external and Dynamics 365 benchmarks. It’s priced for enterprise-scale use, starting at a budget-saving price of $0.01 per audio minute. You can try it out in MAI Labs and register your interest here .

Dragon Copilot Transcribe , built on MAI Transcribe 2, is now live in Dragon Copilot, powering 100% of doctor–patient conversation transcriptions. It covers 10 million encounters a month, halves error rates in multilingual workflows, and is in the hands of a third of US physicians.

Decision 1.1 provides model routing integrated right into your applications so that the bigger, pricier models are only used when you really need them. On the AA Decision Index Microsoft is ahead of Jev, Google and OpenAI, while being faster and cheaper. Used by 4,000 customers, it’s 50x faster and 79x cheaper than GPT-6.1 Sol.

We’ve heard again and again from leaders that no one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model.

And if you build on open weights, can you really trust where they came from, or how they’ll behave when you use one as the foundation for your most valuable IP and data?

We heard you. We started with Custom Models. AT&T developed an MAI custom model for 5G network operation analytics and it outperformed GPT-6.1 Sol at 50x cheaper cost. On complex scenarios, they found that Code 2 delivered frontier-level performance at a significantly lower price than alternatives.

Today, we’re taking a big step forward with MAI Licensed Weights : models under your control.

Take a frontier MAI model, customize it using your proprietary data if you want to. Then run it securely in your own Azure environment.

You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents.

So that’s MAI, a family of world class models with exceptional price performance: the world’s best image editing model; the world’s best transcription model; frontier cyber defense at 2% of the cost; and world class everyday coding models at a price you can scale.

And crucially all of it with Your IQ. Your agents. Your weights. All under your control.

This is Frontier Intelligence you can trust, from the company you can trust.

items.title: Fiona the hippo undergoing care after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo
items.summary: Zookeepers say she cannot have surgery but are providing fluids and supportive care to help her pass the hat.
items.content:
The Cincinnati Zoo in Ohio says its beloved hippopotamus Fiona is undergoing emergency medical care after swallowing a knit hat that slipped into her enclosure.

The Zoo said that Fiona had swallowed the hat about nine days ago and was asymptomatic at first, adding that she was "large enough that a small-ish hat should be passing through".

But a few days later, her appetite started to decrease, and the zoo staff were trying to encourage Fiona to eat to help push the hat through her digestive system.

Fiona rose to fame when she was born premature at the Cincinnati Zoo and at first struggled to survive. Her story inspired an ice cream flavour as well as a character in Cincinnati's ballet.

Michelle Curley, a spokesperson for the zoo, told US media that the hat got into Fiona's enclosure by accident, after a visitor tossed it in the air and it caught on a ceiling fan that flung it through a small opening.

"We probably couldn't make [it] happen again if we tried," Curley said.

Zoo staff have been providing a series of supportive measures like fluids and ultrasounds to help Fiona recover.

The latest ultrasound showed the hat passing through Fiona's small intestine, the staff said, adding that she is still a bit dehydrated.

"Surgery isn't an option for full-grown hippos and our best chance for success with Fiona would be if she could pass this on her own," one of the zookeepers said in an update.

Fiona was born six weeks early to 17-year-old hippo Bibi on 24 January.

At birth she weighed 13 kg (29 lbs), which the zoo said was about half the previous lowest recorded birth weight for her species.

The zoo said staff were "rooting for her and hoping that she proves to be as strong and resilient as she was at the beginning of her life".

items.title: Piani cottura a induzione, il Black Friday di Amazon è già iniziato: ecco le offerte
items.summary: Dai modelli con quattro zone di cottura alle funzioni per velocizzare le preparazioni e contenere i consumi: ecco alcuni piani cottura a induzione già in offerta per il Black Friday ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Il Black Friday di Amazon è già iniziato in anticipo e tra le offerte ci sono anche diversi piani cottura a induzione; una buona occasione per rinnovare la cucina, sostituire un vecchio piano a gas o passare a una soluzione più moderna, con superfici facili da pulire e un controllo preciso della temperatura.

Ecco alcuni modelli in sconto da tenere d'occhio, con prezzi interessanti in offerta in anticipo per il Black Friday.

Il piano cottura a induzione Electrolux Serie 600 LIL63443 ha una larghezza di 60 cm e mette a disposizione quattro zone di cottura, gestibili attraverso i comandi touch con slider.

Una delle sue caratteristiche è la funzione Bridge, che permette di unire due zone in un'unica superficie di cottura, distribuendo il calore in modo uniforme: una soluzione utile quando si utilizzano pentole di grandi dimensioni.

Le zone Infinite, invece, riconoscono le dimensioni della pentola e si adattano alla sua base, così da riscaldarla in modo uniforme sia quando si utilizza una padella piccola sia con una casseruola più grande. Il piano può inoltre funzionare anche con una potenza elettrica disponibile limitata, adattandosi alle caratteristiche dell'impianto domestico.

Non manca la tecnologia Hob2Hood, che permette di collegare il piano in modalità wireless a una cappa Electrolux compatibile: l'aspirazione si attiva e regola automaticamente la propria intensità in base alla cottura.

Il piano cottura a induzione Hisense HI621FM ha una larghezza di 60 cm e dispone di quattro zone di cottura, per una potenza complessiva che arriva a 7.200 W.

La funzione Connect Zone permette di unire due zone da 23 cm, creando un'unica superficie più ampia per utilizzare pentole di grandi dimensioni, bistecchiere o teglie rettangolari, con una distribuzione uniforme del calore.

Per velocizzare le preparazioni ci sono le funzioni Power Boost e Rapid Boil, che aumentano rapidamente la potenza per portare l'acqua a ebollizione o raggiungere in meno tempo la temperatura desiderata.

Tutte le impostazioni si gestiscono attraverso il pannello Touch Control centrale, da cui è possibile regolare la potenza e impostare il timer.

Disponibile in offerta Black Friday al prezzo scontato di 189 euro.

Il piano cottura a induzione Candy Idea è dotato di quattro zone di cottura indipendenti, adatte a pentole e padelle di diverse dimensioni. La tecnologia a induzione riscalda direttamente il fondo delle pentole, riducendo la dispersione di calore e i tempi necessari per cucinare rispetto ai tradizionali piani di cottura.

Per velocizzare ulteriormente le preparazioni è disponibile la funzione Booster, che aumenta temporaneamente la potenza della zona selezionata, ad esempio per portare rapidamente l'acqua a ebollizione.

Un'altra funzione utile è il Power Management, che consente di impostare la potenza massima assorbita dal piano, scegliendo tra 2,5 e 6,6 kW in base alle caratteristiche dell'impianto elettrico e alle proprie esigenze. È presente anche il blocco di sicurezza per bambini, che impedisce l'attivazione accidentale dei comandi. La superficie in vetroceramica nera completa il piano con un design semplice e facile da pulire.

Il piano a induzione Candy Idea è ora scontato al prezzo di 165 euro.

Il Bosch Serie 4 PUE611BB5J è un piano cottura a induzione da 60 cm con quattro zone di cottura, progettato per rendere più semplici e veloci le preparazioni quotidiane.

La funzione PowerBoost permette di aumentare temporaneamente la potenza fino al 50% rispetto al livello massimo standard, riducendo i tempi necessari, ad esempio, per portare l'acqua a ebollizione. I comandi TouchSelect consentono di selezionare la zona desiderata e regolare la potenza con un semplice tocco, utilizzando i tasti + e -.

Il piano integra anche un timer che, una volta raggiunto il tempo impostato, spegne automaticamente la zona di cottura selezionata. In caso di spegnimento accidentale, inoltre, la funzione di riavvio permette di recuperare le impostazioni precedenti e riprendere la preparazione.

Non manca il blocco di sicurezza per bambini, che impedisce modifiche involontarie ai comandi. Il piano misura 59,2 x 52,2 cm e richiede un vano di incasso da 56 x 49-50 cm.

Ora in offerta per il Black Friday anticipato al prezzo di 215 euro

items.title: KTM rubata durante EICMA: lo stunt rider Bagoros la ritrova grazie ad un fan
items.summary: Rubata fuori da EICMA 2026 la KTM 1390 Super Duke R dello stuntman sloveno Rok Bagoros. Decisivo l'aiuto di un appassionato italiano e della Polizia di Stato per il recupero.
items.content:
Una videochiamata partita dall'Italia, lo schermo dello smartphone che si accende e sullo sfondo la sua KTM 1390 Super Duke R EVO, intera, senza neppure un graffio. Rok Bagoros è scoppiato a piangere così, una settimana esatta dopo aver salutato Milano con i vetri del furgone sfondati e la convinzione di non rivedere mai più la sua moto. A riportargliela in garage non sono stati soltanto gli agenti della Polizia di Stato, ma soprattutto Andrea, un motociclista italiano che fino alla sera del furto lo stunt rider sloveno non aveva mai incontrato e che ha deciso di prendersi a cuore quella ricerca come fosse roba sua.Per la cronaca Rok Bagoros è lo stunt rider ufficiale della casa di Mattighofen dal 2011 circa e oggi è il volto che KTM usa più spesso per mostrare la gamma delle sue naked stradali. Purtroppo dopo la trasferta a EICMA, però, il suo nome torna a circolare per un motivo che avrebbe evitato volentieri.

Il furto alla Bicocca e la caccia fino all'alba

I guai per Bagoros erano cominciati sabato 8 novembre intorno alle 21:30 nella zona del Bicocca Village, periferia nord di Milano. Arrivato in città per EICMA con più moto al seguito, aveva lasciato chiusa nel proprio furgone la sua Super Duke, una naked da 190 CV che supera abbondantemente i 20.000 euro di valore. I ladri hanno mandato in frantumi i finestrini e l'hanno portata via.
 
Visualizza questo post su Instagram
 

Un post condiviso da RokBagoros | freestyle moto (@rokbagoros)

Scoperto il furto, lo stunt sloveno ha pubblicato subito sui social le foto dei cristalli spaccati e della moto, offrendo 3.000 euro di ricompensa per qualsiasi informazione utile. Il post ha iniziato a rimbalzare tra migliaia di appassionati italiani fino ad arrivare ad Andrea. I due si sono sentiti e quella notte stessa hanno battuto le strade di Milano fino alle quattro del mattino cercando tracce, ma all'alba non era ancora saltato fuori niente. La domenica Bagoros è stato costretto a ripartire: doveva caricare le altre moto dalla fiera e guidare nove ore fino in Slovenia, dove lo aspettava la moglie agli ultimi giorni di gravidanza. Lasciare Milano a mani vuote, ha raccontato lui stesso, è stato uno strazio.

Le indagini in Questura e il rientro in Slovenia

Partito Bagoros, Andrea non ha lasciato perdere. Si è presentato negli uffici della Questura di Milano e ha continuato a lavorare fianco a fianco con i poliziotti, tenendo aggiornato lo sloveno giorno dopo giorno su ogni singolo indizio emerso in città. Sette giorni dopo il colpo è arrivata la chiamata decisiva: Andrea era in compagnia degli agenti e dietro di loro c'era la KTM, intatta. Bagoros non ha perso un minuto ed è ripartito verso l'Italia insieme al fratello. Il giorno seguente avevano già recuperato la moto e in meno di 24 ore la Super Duke era di nuovo parcheggiata dentro l'officina slovena. Non sono stati svelati il luogo preciso del ritrovamento né l'eventuale presenza di fermati, ma il pilota ha voluto condividere anche il messaggio ricevuto successivamente da uno dei poliziotti della squadra, rimasto colpito dall'emozione dello sloveno al momento della riconsegna. Nei suoi ringraziamenti finali Bagoros ha citato chiunque abbia condiviso l'appello, gli agenti e soprattutto Andrea, riassumendo tutto in una frase: essere tornato a casa con la propria moto ma anche con nuovi amici, il vero significato della community motociclistica.Un epilogo ben diverso rispetto a quanto capitato a Scott Redding sempre in occasione di EICMA 2026: durante il viaggio di ritorno verso casa, due furgoni del pilota britannico sono stati forzati in Francia e i ladri hanno portato via una mountain bike che al momento non risulta ancora ritrovata.
